edition: Newton, Principia, Andrew Motte trans., 1729 (Wikisource); Axioms, or Laws of Motion, Law II.

figures.caption: Law II --- The alteration of motion is ever proportional to the motive force impressed; and is made in the direction of the right line in which that force is impressed.

text.latex: \textcolor{motion}{The alteration of motion} is ever proportional to the \textcolor{force}{motive force impress'd}: "if any \textcolor{force}{force} generates a \textcolor{motion}{motion}, a double \textcolor{force}{force} will generate double the \textcolor{motion}{motion}," and a triple \textcolor{force}{force} triple the \textcolor{motion}{motion}. This holds whether the \textcolor{force}{force} be impress'd altogether and at once, or gradually and successively. The exact scaling is the heart of the law --- $\textcolor{motion}{\Delta(\text{motion})} \propto \textcolor{force}{F}$ --- the seed from which $F = ma$ grows.

The \textcolor{line}{alteration is made in the direction of the right line} in which that \textcolor{force}{force} is impress'd --- \textcolor{line}{always directed the same way} with the generating \textcolor{force}{force}. If the body \textcolor{old}{moved before}, this new \textcolor{line}{motion} is added to or subducted from the \textcolor{old}{former motion}, according as they directly conspire or are directly contrary. When they are \textcolor{line}{obliquely joyned}, the \textcolor{force}{force} and the \textcolor{old}{prior motion} compound by the parallelogram rule, so as to produce a new \textcolor{line}{motion compounded from the determination of both} --- hence $\textcolor{line}{\Delta(\text{motion})} \parallel \textcolor{force}{F}$.
